newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UES plans 3-yr convertible bond on 2.7 pct shares.
newsitem.headline: UES plans 3-yr convertible bond on 2.7 pct shares.

text.p: Russia's national power company Unified Energy System (UES) plans to start a convertible bond programme covering 2.7 percent of its shares by autumn, UES chief executive Boris Brevnov said on Thursday, adding that the bonds would not be issued all at once.
"The government will keep 50 percent plus one share (of UES)," he said. The government holds 52.7 percent of shares in the company now.
"The rest (2.7 percent) will be used as convertible bonds," Brevnon told a news conference.
He said the bonds will be convertible in about three years.
Brevnov said the convertible bonds would be interest-bearing, and that a government order on the bond issue was almost ready. Final approval was expected within the next few days, he added.

He said that UES would issue regulation 144-A American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), to allow foreign trading of UES shares, before the bonds were issued. UES has said that the ADR issue would boost the company's share price.
UES shares on the Russian Trading System were last traded at $0.4495 at 1235 GMT, up sharply from Wednesday's close of $0.4055, but well below Thursday's intraday peak of $0.4650.
